title: Man. Post. Cap. X: PLAC — ‘you eat / you die’ both address Adam, not all posterity
pass_a_gloss: Nothing in the threat’s words lets it cover others than those the mandate covers. ‘In the day you eat of it, you shall die.’ Who does not see that both ‘you eat’ and ‘you die’ address the same person—not ‘die’ to all men and ‘eat’ to Adam alone?
pass_b_english: For there is nothing in the words of the threat from which it can be deduced that it looks to others than those to whom the mandate or ban looks.
In the day you eat of it, you shall die the death.
Who does not see that both that word you eat and you die look to the same person—not this to all men, and that to Adam alone?
source_text: Nihil enim est in verbis comminationis, ex quo deduci possit, eam ad alios spectare, quam ad quos spectat mandatum seu interdictum. Quo die comederis ex ea, morte morieris. Quis non videt ad eandem personam utrumque illud verbum comederis & morieris spectare, non autem hoc ad omnes homines, illud ad solum Adamum?

choices.choice: Eat and die address Adam alone
